messages.author: a36543cbca755a88
messages.subject: Re: To show labels on scatterplot with mouse click
parts: If you're trying to add interactivity to a plot created with base functions or ggplot2, yes, you have to do some fancy calculations and it's unlikely to be worth while.  You will find it easier if you swap to a different means of generating the graphic, using a package like {ggvis}, {googleVis} or {rcharts}.  If you're used to ggplot2 you'll find the transition to ggvis easiest.  googleVis is the most mature of the three but has some idiosyncratic data shape requirements and customisation/polishing often takes you straight into javascript; rcharts opens up a big world of options but doesn't have a consistent approach or enough documentation yet.  Whichever you choose you can still have Shiny deliver the fundamental interactivity, and the ggvis or whatever provides micro-interactivity (ie tooltips).  In fact ggvis works with Shiny in the background server-side even for tooltips but this doesn't seem to impact too much on performance.
